title: How to Grill Sliced Peaches and Burrata on a Non-Stick Mat
meta_description: Learn how to master grilling peaches on grill mat for the perfect summer appetizer. Pair charred peaches with creamy burrata for a gourmet treat.
html:
There is something magical about the combination of warm, caramelized fruit and cold, creamy cheese. Grilled peaches and burrata is one of those dishes that looks like it belongs in a high-end bistro but takes less than fifteen minutes to pull together in your own backyard.

The challenge has always been the fruit itself. Peaches are delicate; they soften quickly and often slide through grill grates or stick to the metal, leaving you with a charred mess instead of a beautiful slice. That is why I swear by grilling peaches on grill mat. Using BBQ Grill Mats allows you to get those gorgeous sear marks without the risk of the fruit collapsing or sticking to the grill.

Why Use BBQ Grill Mats for Delicate Fruit?

If you've ever tried to grill sliced peaches directly on the grates, you know the struggle. The natural sugars in the fruit caramelize instantly, which sounds great, but it often creates a "glue" effect. You go to flip the peach, and half of it stays stuck to the grill.

BBQ Grill Mats act as a protective barrier. They distribute heat evenly and prevent flare-ups caused by dripping fruit juices. Because they are non-stick, the peaches slide right off once they've reached that perfect golden-brown state. Plus, it keeps the cleanup simple—you just wipe down the mat rather than scrubbing the entire grill surface.

Choosing and Prepping Your Peaches

For this recipe, you want peaches that are ripe but still firm. If they are too soft, they will turn into mush the moment they hit the heat. Look for fruit that gives slightly under gentle pressure but doesn't feel "squishy."

To prep them, slice the peaches in half and remove the pit. I prefer slicing them into thick wedges—about 3/4 of an inch—to ensure they hold their shape. Before they hit the grill, lightly brush the cut side of each slice with a neutral oil (like grapeseed or avocado oil) or a bit of melted butter. This enhances the caramelization and adds an extra layer of protection against sticking.

Step-by-Step: Grilling Peaches on Grill Mat

Follow these steps to get a professional char without the stress:

  1. Preheat: Get your grill to medium-high heat (around 375°F to 400°F). Once hot, lay your BBQ Grill Mats directly on the grates.
  2. Placement: Carefully place your oiled peach slices onto the mat. Don't crowd them; leave a little space between each slice so the heat can circulate.
  3. The First Sear: Let the peaches grill undisturbed for 3 to 5 minutes. Resist the urge to move them; this is how you get those distinct, appetizing grill marks.
  4. The Flip: Using a wide spatula, gently flip the slices. Grill for another 3 to 4 minutes on the second side.
  5. Check for Doneness: The peaches should be tender and have deep golden-brown char marks but should still hold their shape when lifted.

Assembling the Burrata Platter

While the peaches are grilling, prepare your base. Place a ball of fresh burrata cheese in the center of a serving platter. Use a knife or fork to gently break the outer skin of the burrata, allowing the creamy center (stracciatella) to spill out slightly.

Arrange the warm, grilled peaches around the cheese. The contrast of the hot fruit against the cold cheese is what makes this dish a winner. To finish, drizzle the entire platter with a high-quality balsamic glaze or honey. I love adding a sprinkle of flaky sea salt and a handful of fresh basil leaves or mint for a pop of color and freshness.

Pro Tips for the Best Results

If you want to take this dish from a side to a showstopper, try adding a few toasted pine nuts or slivered almonds for crunch. The creaminess of the burrata and the softness of the peaches benefit greatly from a contrasting texture.

Regarding your gear, remember that BBQ Grill Mats are reusable. After your meal, let the mat cool slightly, then wash it with warm soapy water. Avoid using metal scrubbers on the mat to preserve the non-stick surface for your next summer cookout.

FAQ

Can I use frozen peaches for this recipe?

I don't recommend it. Frozen peaches have a higher moisture content and a softer texture once thawed, which makes them likely to fall apart on the grill, even when using a mat.

What other fruits work well with BBQ Grill Mats?

Almost any stone fruit or firm fruit works great! Try pineapple rings, nectarines, or halved plums. The non-stick surface is perfect for anything with high sugar content that typically sticks to metal.

How do I know if my grill is too hot?

If the peaches are turning black/burnt on the outside but are still raw and hard in the middle, your heat is too high. Aim for a medium-high heat to ensure the sugars caramelize slowly and evenly.
